spec_match.rationale: Exercises startRendering(chunkSize) as a pull loop with the explainer's close()-based feature detection, and renders a real graph on every build.

interactive.rationale: Length/chunk inputs, create/next/all buttons, a chunks table, a live waveform canvas with text equivalent, and an explanatory output region.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises the requested-vs-received comparison with the honest ignored-argument outcome; delivered exactly (requested 4096, received 16000 on this build).

edge_cases.rationale: Covers ignored-argument, auto-closed-context rejection on further pulls, and the attribute-missing support banner.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/<id> plus the exact spec anchor in see-also.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite pins bounded chunks, repeatability, auto-close across >=2 pulls, close() behaviour, indefinite constructibility, and classic one-shot compatibility; verified executing (1 pass / 7 fail here - the compatibility assertion passes, correctly).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Verified on headless Chromium 141 (predates Chrome 158, feature absent even behind --enable-experimental-web-platform-features) via Playwright 1.56 at desktop 1280x800 and mobile 360x740 DPR3 touch, driving every control; screenshots under /tmp/claude-0/agentB/shots/. Real audio rendered: table showed requested 4096 / received 16000 amber-flagged, waveform drew 16000 frames with peak 0.776, state closed; a bounded multi-pull run needs a 158 build.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry.assert covers the primary contract and the explicit fallback branch; console output is intentional and prefixed.

design_system.rationale: Only CSS variables from public/styles.css; buttons overriding background also set color; AA pairs (text-charcoal/bg-stone, bg-ivory/text-black, accent-emerald-dark on paper).

accessibility.rationale: Native controls with labels, visible focus (verified first-Tab), caption+scope tables, aria-live polite result regions.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Mobile overflow found during verification (long API token in the support banner) and fixed with overflow-wrap anywhere + min-width 0; re-verified clean at 360px.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify the supported path on a real Chrome 158 / Canary build
openQuestions.detail: This environment's Chromium 141 lacks the surface even behind --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, so only the honest-absent branch ran. On Chrome 158 (or Canary with the feature's runtime flag) verify: received === requested per pull, multiple pulls, and the context auto-closing only after the final chunk.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsically-sized grid/flex layouts (auto-fit + minmax) so panels reflow without horizontal overflow at narrow widths.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Control panels use grid-template-columns repeat(auto-fit, minmax()), tables are wrapped in overflow-x containers, and long tokens use overflow-wrap: anywhere; verified no horizontal overflow at 360px.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Landmarks, native semantics, accessible names, visible focus, and polite live regions for asynchronous state changes.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Content sits in main/header/footer landmarks; async results land in aria-live=polite output/status elements; tables carry caption plus th scope=col; first-Tab focus visibility verified in the browser.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use native labelled controls with adequate touch targets and visible hints for constraints.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: All controls are native button/select/input/radio elements with <label for> associations, min-height 44px, and inline constraint hints.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Expose canvas content to assistive tech, e.g. via HTML-in-canvas (layoutsubtree).
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Exception recorded: layoutsubtree/HTML-in-canvas is itself experimental and unavailable on the verification build, so the guidance's fallback strategy is used instead - canvas has role=img with aria-labelledby/aria-describedby and a text equivalent (frame count, duration, peak amplitude) updated on every draw.

summary: Real rendering on every build with the requested-vs-received row as the honest support signal.
